events.title: Pound Slides After U.K. Economic Data
events.description: The British pound weakened against other major currencies in the European session on Wednesday, following the United Kingdom's (UK) mixed inflation-related data releases.

events.title: European Shares Mixed In Cautious Trade
events.description: European stocks were little changed on Wednesday after falling the most in eight months in the previous session on concerns over the artificial intelligence trade.

events.title: Pound Slides Against Majors
events.description: The British pound weakened against other major currencies in the European session on Wednesday.

events.title: Asian Shares Mixed Despite Nvidia Earnings Beat
events.description: Asian stocks ended mixed on Wednesday despite Wall Street facing a fresh wave of selling pressure overnight on concerns over the artificial intelligence trade and expectations of more aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.

events.title: Malaysia GDP Growth Beats Estimate
events.description: Malaysia's economy grew faster than anticipated in the third quarter with investment and exports serving as key drivers of expansion, official data revealed Wednesday. Gross domestic product expanded 5.5 percent year-on-year, the Department of Statistics said. The rate surpassed the advance estimate of 5.3 percent but came in weaker than the second quarter's 6.0 percent expansion.

events.title: European Shares Set For Softer Open Ahead Of Fed Minutes
events.description: European stocks are seen opening mostly lower on Wednesday as investors await the release of minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting later in the day for clues as to whether policymakers are leaning towards another rate increase next month.

events.title: Indian Shares Modestly Lower In Early Trade
events.description: Indian shares opened a tad lower on Wednesday as weak global cues, hawkish Fed remarks and rising tensions in the Middle East prompted traders to lock in profits after recent strong gains.

events.title: Australian Market Extends Early Losses In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is extending its early losses in mid-market moves on Wednesday, adding to the losses in the previous four sessions, with the benchmark S&P/ASX 200 falling well below the 8,900 level, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, with weakness in financial and energy stocks partially offset by gains in mining stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets Track Wall Street Lower
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly lower on Wednesday, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, as rising oil prices renewed concerns about global inflation risk and interest rate hikes amid increasing tensions in the Middle East after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday.

events.title: Indian Shares Seen Lower After Recent Rally
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening slightly lower on Wednesday, a day after the benchmark Nifty hit a nine-month high, driven by strong banking sector performance and gains in crude-sensitive sectors.

events.title: Thai Stock Market May Take Further Damage On Wednesday
events.description: The Thai stock market has tracked lower in two straight sessions, shedding more than 30 points or 2 percent along the way. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just beneath the 1,475-point plateau and it's expected to open under pressure again on Wednesday.

events.title: Japanese Market Modestly Higher
events.description: The Japanese stock market is trading modestly higher on Wednesday, reversing some of the sharp losses in the previous two sessions, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is moving above the 59,000 level, with gains in index heavyweights and a mixed performance across most other sectors.

events.title: Australian Market Modestly Lower
events.description: Australian shares are trading modestly lower on Wednesday, extending the losses in the previous four sessions, with the benchmark S&P/ASX 200 falling well below the 8,900 level, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, with weakness in financial and energy stocks partially offset by gains in mining stocks.
